sentences.en: Driving into the suburbs, going to a Panera in Westerville.
sentences.zh: 开车去郊区，去韦斯特维尔的一家Panera餐厅。

sentences.en: It's probably a no better spot to anchor a story on suburban voters than a Panera.
sentences.zh: 对于报道郊区选民的故事来说，Panera大概是再好不过的切入点了。

sentences.en: Okay, what's the deal with Panera?
sentences.zh: 好吧，Panera到底有什么特别之处？

sentences.en: Actually, in 2018, strategists would talk to me a lot about the Panera voter.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在2018年，策略师们经常跟我谈论“Panera选民”。

sentences.en: The kinds of suburbs that have really shown the biggest switch have been these sort of inner ring,
sentences.zh: 那些真正表现出最大转变的郊区，往往是这种内环的、

sentences.en: maybe more affluent suburban communities, and there's a lot of Paneras in those places.
sentences.zh: 可能更富裕的郊区社区，而这些地方有很多Panera餐厅。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, this is The Field.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》的《现场》栏目。

sentences.en: I'm Lisa Lair in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我是俄亥俄州的丽莎·莱尔。

sentences.en: I get some water.
sentences.zh: 我去拿点水。

sentences.en: I'm Lisa.
sentences.zh: 我是丽莎。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: I recognize you from your photo.
sentences.zh: 我从照片上认出你了。

sentences.en: So a few weeks ago, my colleague Jessica Chung and I went to the suburbs of Columbus to meet someone for lunch at the outdoor patio of a Panera bread.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我和同事杰西卡·钟去了哥伦布市的郊区，在一家Panera Bread的户外露台上与人共进午餐。

sentences.en: Everybody likes Panera.
sentences.zh: 每个人都喜欢Panera。

sentences.en: Which, admittedly, was a little on the nose.
sentences.zh: 不得不承认，这有点太刻意了。

sentences.en: And it's delicious.
sentences.zh: 而且它很好吃。

sentences.en: We are going to meet a woman who, in our reporting on the suburbs and the much-discussed suburban women vote, both Jess and I independently had heard about.
sentences.zh: 我们要见一位女性，在我和杰西关于郊区以及备受讨论的“郊区女性选票”的报道中，我们俩都曾独立听说过她。

sentences.en: I'm Katie Paris.
sentences.zh: 我是凯蒂·帕里斯。
我41岁。

sentences.en: I live in Shaker Heights, which is a suburb outside of Cleveland.
sentences.zh: 我住在谢克海茨，那是克利夫兰郊外的一个社区。

sentences.en: And I am working to flip Ohio blue in 2020.
sentences.zh: 我正在努力让俄亥俄州在2020年变蓝。

sentences.en: Katie is a lifelong Democrat who started her career in national politics.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂是一位终身民主党人，她的职业生涯始于国家政治。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I met my husband in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是在华盛顿特区遇到我丈夫的，

sentences.en: about 18 years ago.
sentences.zh: 大约18年前。

sentences.en: And I think I knew by the end of our second date that I might just be moving to Ohio one day.
sentences.zh: 我想在第二次约会结束时，我就知道自己有一天可能会搬到俄亥俄州去。

sentences.en: Her husband grew up in Ohio, and they moved back to start a family there.
sentences.zh: 她丈夫在俄亥俄州长大，他们搬回那里组建了家庭。

sentences.en: But Katie kept commuting to D.C.
sentences.zh: 但凯蒂仍然通勤到华盛顿特区

sentences.en: for work.
sentences.zh: 工作。

sentences.en: In 2016, when Donald Trump was elected, she just had her first son.
sentences.zh: 2016年，唐纳德·特朗普当选时，她刚生下第一个儿子。

sentences.en: I felt worried, and I felt kind of like a pissed-off mom.
sentences.zh: 我感到很担心，感觉自己像个愤怒的妈妈。

sentences.en: Then comes 2018 and the midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 接着是2018年的中期选举。

sentences.en: Where, of course, we saw this blue wave that flipped the House back to the Democrats and put a bunch of women into office.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们看到了那股让众议院重回民主党掌控、并将许多女性送入公职的“蓝色浪潮”。

sentences.en: But in Katie's home state of Ohio, that wasn't what happened.
sentences.zh: 但在凯蒂的家乡俄亥俄州，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: Ohio Democrats had not picked up a single congressional seat.
sentences.zh: 俄亥俄州的民主党人没有赢得一个国会席位。

sentences.en: And that was a very different story than many other parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 这与全国其他许多地方的情况截然不同。

sentences.en: Just up in Michigan, they elected an all-female statewide ticket, flipped congressional seats.
sentences.zh: 就在密歇根州，他们选出了全女性的州级候选人名单，并翻转了国会席位。

sentences.en: I mean, 43 seats, I think, in the end flipped.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最终有43个席位发生了翻转，我想。

sentences.en: 38 of them were suburban districts.
sentences.zh: 其中38个是郊区选区。

sentences.en: And I began thinking, well, why didn't that happen in Ohio?
sentences.zh: 我开始思考，为什么俄亥俄州没有发生这种情况？

sentences.en: And so I think it was the morning after the 2018 election, I remember, like, getting dressed for the day,
sentences.zh: 我想那是2018年选举后的第二天早上，我记得当时正在穿衣准备出门，

sentences.en: talking to my husband, and just saying, I think I might need to make a change.
sentences.zh: 和丈夫交谈，我说，我想我可能需要做出改变。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel right anymore to be not focused on Ohio.
sentences.zh: 不再专注于俄亥俄州感觉不对劲了。

sentences.en: So what kind of change did you make?
sentences.zh: 那么你做了什么样的改变？

sentences.en: Well, I had no idea what that was going to mean yet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时还不知道那意味着什么。

sentences.en: But I knew there was, like, a thing that had happened with suburban women that had done a lot of good in other places.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，郊区女性身上发生了一些事情，在其他地方产生了很好的效果。

sentences.en: She knew that the blue wave in other states was due in part to a shift among suburban women.
sentences.zh: 她知道其他州的蓝色浪潮在一定程度上归功于郊区女性的转变。

sentences.en: And that resonated with me, particularly at a personal level, because here I am as a mom raising my kids in a suburb.
sentences.zh: 这引起了我的共鸣，特别是在个人层面上，因为我就是一个在郊区抚养孩子的妈妈。

sentences.en: And so I thought, I was really drawn to this power of women engaging in politics.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我真的被女性参与政治的力量所吸引。

sentences.en: And I just wanted a piece of that, you know, and to sort of figure out what that would mean here in Ohio, because it seemed really powerful.
sentences.zh: 我只是想参与其中，你知道，想弄清楚这在俄亥俄州意味着什么，因为它看起来真的很强大。

sentences.en: In this election year, it can seem like the country is impossibly divided.
sentences.zh: 在这个选举年，国家看起来似乎陷入了不可调和的分裂。

sentences.en: And it's hard to imagine any group of voters changing their minds.
sentences.zh: 很难想象任何选民群体会改变主意。

sentences.en: But there's one big exception to that, and that's suburban white women.
sentences.zh: 但有一个巨大的例外，那就是郊区白人女性。

sentences.en: In 2016, it was their surprising support for Trump that helped push him over the edge.
sentences.zh: 2016年，正是她们对特朗普令人惊讶的支持，帮助他取得了胜利。

sentences.en: But in the last four years, they've changed their minds in astonishing numbers.
sentences.zh: 但在过去的四年里，她们以惊人的数量改变了主意。

sentences.en: The midterms were the first real signal.
sentences.zh: 中期选举是第一个真正的信号。

sentences.en: But now, polling shows that while the race between Trump and Biden is evenly split among suburban men, suburban women favor Biden by 23 points.
sentences.zh: 但现在，民调显示，虽然特朗普和拜登在郊区男性中的支持率旗鼓相当，但郊区女性以23个百分点的优势支持拜登。

sentences.en: That means that the same group that helped give Trump his seat could take it away.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，正是那个帮助特朗普赢得席位的群体，现在可能会夺走它。

sentences.en: But will it happen in the swing state of Ohio, which bucked the trend in 2018 and is a must-win for Republicans this year?
sentences.zh: 但这会发生在摇摆州俄亥俄州吗？该州在2018年违背了这一趋势，也是共和党今年必须赢下的州。

sentences.en: In 2016, Trump won there by 8 points.
sentences.zh: 2016年，特朗普在那里以8个百分点的优势获胜。

sentences.en: But now, the race is very, very close.
sentences.zh: 但现在，竞争非常、非常激烈。

sentences.en: I just had that mama bear sort of response, you know.
sentences.zh: 我当时就有了那种“护犊子”的反应，你知道的。

sentences.en: So, after this wake-up call that Katie has following the 2018 midterMs...
sentences.zh: 所以，在凯蒂经历2018年中期选举的警钟之后……

sentences.en: I didn't know enough.
sentences.zh: 我了解得不够多。

sentences.en: I wanted to learn more, so...
sentences.zh: 我想了解更多，所以……

sentences.en: She starts by looking at the data from Ohio.
sentences.zh: 她开始查看俄亥俄州的数据。

sentences.en: But first of all, I didn't know that Black voters in Ohio are doing the work, like, carrying a disproportionate share of the burden here.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我不知道俄亥俄州的黑人选民正在努力工作，承担了这里不成比例的重担。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, people who look like me, living in the suburbs, we are not.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，像我这样住在郊区的人，却没有这样做。

sentences.en: What she found was that not only did white suburban women in Ohio turn out for Democrats far less reliably than Black women did,
sentences.zh: 她发现，俄亥俄州的郊区白人女性不仅在支持民主党方面远不如黑人女性可靠，

sentences.en: they also just turned out to vote less in general, in lower numbers.
sentences.zh: 而且她们总体的投票率也更低，人数更少。

sentences.en: And so the obvious way to change an election was to fix both those probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以改变选举结果的显而易见的方法就是解决这两个问题。

sentences.en: Um, and, you know, I just thought, that's not going to magically happen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我只是觉得，这不会奇迹般地发生。

sentences.en: I've seen, I've seen this data, I can't unsee it, I have to do something.
sentences.zh: 我看到了，我看到了这些数据，我无法假装没看见，我必须做点什么。

sentences.en: So in 2019, Katie quits her job in D.C.
sentences.zh: 于是2019年，凯蒂辞去了在华盛顿特区的工作，

sentences.en: and starts focusing on this full-time.
sentences.zh: 开始全职专注于这件事。

sentences.en: And so that's when I started traveling around the state, talking to suburban women, especially in these fast-growing suburbs of Columbus.
sentences.zh: 所以那时我开始在全州范围内奔走，与郊区女性交谈，特别是在哥伦布市这些快速发展的郊区。

sentences.en: And that was when I started meeting women in places like Panera.
sentences.zh: 也就是那时，我开始在Panera之类的地方结识女性。

sentences.en: At first, she's just using social media to identify groups of Democratic women
sentences.zh: 起初，她只是利用社交媒体来识别民主党女性群体，

sentences.en: who have come together locally around a shared but growing sense of despair over the Trump presidency.
sentences.zh: 这些女性因对特朗普总统任期的共同但日益增长的绝望感而在当地聚集在一起。

sentences.en: And a desire to do something.
sentences.zh: 以及想要做点什么的愿望。

sentences.en: Meeting up with women over wine or coffee and hearing their stories in their suburbs,
sentences.zh: 和女性们喝着红酒或咖啡见面，听她们在郊区的故事，

sentences.en: women who had never been involved in politics, no interest in politics before the 2016 election, and feeling sort of, like, isolated in their suburbs, too.
sentences.zh: 那些在2016年大选前从未参与过政治、对政治毫无兴趣的女性，也感到在郊区有些孤立。

sentences.en: Like, thinking, it feels like it's mostly Republicans around here.
sentences.zh: 比如，心想，这附近好像大多是共和党人。

sentences.en: You know, I'm just, I'm going to be quiet about my views.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我还是对自己的观点保持沉默吧。

sentences.en: Reaching out to maybe a few other women who they thought might think like them.
sentences.zh: 联系可能和她们想法一致的其他几位女性。

sentences.en: Getting together at the Panera.
sentences.zh: 在Panera聚会。

sentences.en: And Katie watches as these groups grow, just through word of mouth.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂看着这些群体通过口碑不断壮大。

sentences.en: They would say, let's do this again next week.
sentences.zh: 她们会说，下周再聚吧。

sentences.en: You know, let's do it again.
sentences.zh: 你知道，再聚一次。

sentences.en: And each time, more women would show up.
sentences.zh: 每一次，都会有更多的女性出现。

sentences.en: And so then they would say, let's create a secret Facebook group so that we can keep this conversation going day in and day out.
sentences.zh: 于是她们会说，让我们创建一个秘密的Facebook群组，这样我们就可以日复一日地保持对话。

sentences.en: And then those groups would start with, like, 25 women in them.
sentences.zh: 然后这些群组开始时大约有25名女性。

sentences.en: And then they would grow to 50.
sentences.zh: 接着增长到50人。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, I mean, all of these groups now have anywhere from 200 to 1,000 women in them.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我的意思是，所有这些群组现在都有200到1000名女性成员。

sentences.en: Can you tell us the names of some of these groups?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们其中一些群组的名字吗？

sentences.en: Uh, yeah, so Bay Village nasty women.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，比如“海湾村讨厌的女人”。

sentences.en: Grrr, as in, like, grassroots resistance.
sentences.zh: Grrr，意思是基层抵抗。

sentences.en: But they call themselves grrr, and you have to growl when you say it because it just represents, like, that they're mad all the time about everything going on.
sentences.zh: 但她们自称为“Grrr”，你说的时候还得发出低吼声，因为它代表了她们对正在发生的一切一直感到愤怒。

sentences.en: At a certain point, Katie decides to start her own group.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，凯蒂决定成立自己的群组。

sentences.en: A kind of statewide super group.
sentences.zh: 一种全州范围的超级群组。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, what if we connected all of these women together so they could share all of their best ideas?
sentences.zh: 我想，如果我们把所有这些女性联系在一起，让她们分享彼此最好的想法会怎样？

sentences.en: And if we tapped into their voices and their networks to make this whole thing way bigger than it is right now, just within their...
sentences.zh: 如果我们利用她们的声音和人脉，让这一切变得比现在大得多，不仅仅是在她们的……

sentences.en: She called her group...
sentences.zh: 她把她的群组称为……

sentences.en: She called her red wine and blue.
sentences.zh: 她称之为“红酒与蓝色”。

sentences.en: Red wine and blue.
sentences.zh: 红酒与蓝色。

sentences.en: I thought their voices were so interesting because they were just not your typical political activiSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她们的声音非常有趣，因为她们根本不是你典型的政治活动家。

sentences.en: Didn't look or sound like a political activist that you would typically think of.
sentences.zh: 看起来或听起来都不像你通常认为的政治活动家。

sentences.en: And so I thought they were really relatable, that other moms would connect with their stories.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为她们真的很亲切，其他妈妈会与她们的故事产生共鸣。

sentences.en: Because politics can feel really polarizing and divisive and, like, you don't want to be that girl, you know, talking about politics.
sentences.zh: 因为政治可能会让人感到非常两极分化和分裂，而且，你知道，你不想成为那个谈论政治的女孩。

sentences.en: So how could we change that?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何改变这一点呢？

sentences.en: And I thought, these women's voices are key to that.
sentences.zh: 我想，这些女性的声音是关键。

sentences.en: This is the big thing in Katie's mind, is how different these women are from what you typically expect from a political organizer.
sentences.zh: 在凯蒂看来，最重要的一点是，这些女性与你通常期望的政治组织者有多么不同。

sentences.en: Typical paid political organizers are under the age of 25.
sentences.zh: 典型的付费政治组织者年龄都在25岁以下。

sentences.en: They are trained with talking points and scripts and very specific ways of doing things.
sentences.zh: 她们接受过谈话要点、脚本和非常具体的做事方式的培训。

sentences.en: They probably are not talking a lot about vulnerability and courage.
sentences.zh: 她们可能不会谈论太多关于脆弱性和勇气的话题。

sentences.en: They're probably...
sentences.zh: 她们可能……

sentences.en: And they definitely don't get to drink as much wine.
sentences.zh: 而且她们绝对喝不了那么多酒。

sentences.en: They're usually from out of town.
sentences.zh: 她们通常来自外地。

sentences.en: You know, unlike our women, who have lived in these communities for 15 years, probably on average, some longer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不像我们的女性，她们在这些社区平均住了15年，有的更久。

sentences.en: And, you know, like, they're known as, like, the mom to text if there's, like, something going on with the schools about whatever.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，她们被认为是那种如果学校发生什么事，可以发短信询问的妈妈。

sentences.en: So that is not your typical paid political organizer, to say the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，至少可以说，那不是你典型的付费政治组织者。

sentences.en: And I thought the other key thing about them, besides their voices, were who they knew.
sentences.zh: 我认为她们的另一个关键点，除了她们的声音，就是她们认识的人。

sentences.en: I mean, I just thought, the contacts each of these women have in their phones, like, there's so much power here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我只是觉得，这些女性手机通讯录里的联系人，这里面蕴含着巨大的力量。

sentences.en: Contained in the contacts of each of these women are potentially dozens of other women in their communities who may or may not have voted Democratic in 2016,
sentences.zh: 在这些女性的联系人中，可能包含着她们社区里几十位其他女性，她们可能在2016年投了民主党，也可能没有，

sentences.en: but who may be open to it this year.
sentences.zh: 但今年可能对民主党持开放态度。

sentences.en: As data-driven as you try to make any campaign, data is always imperfect.
sentences.zh: 无论你试图让竞选活动多么数据驱动，数据总是不完美的。

sentences.en: What is pretty darn good, though, is what these women know about other women in their community.

sentences.zh: 这与其说是关于具体的政策或总统所做或所说的某件具体事情。

sentences.zh: 活动家，当然。

sentences.zh: 我只是，我是一个有情感的妈妈，那种强烈的情感，你懂吗？

sentences.zh: 所以，是的，2016年之后我经历了一段心路历程……

sentences.en: Andrea says this is a totally new kind of experience for her, too.
sentences.zh: 安德里亚说，这对她来说也是一种全新的体验。

sentences.en: I've, in the last just like six months, have really pushed myself hard outside of my comfort zone to really speak out, like on social media.
sentences.zh: 在过去短短六个月里，我真的强迫自己走出舒适区，去大声疾呼，比如在社交媒体上。

sentences.en: I never touched politics before on social media and with other folks, too.
sentences.zh: 我以前从不在社交媒体上触碰政治，和其他人也是如此。

sentences.en: Like, I have a Biden sticker on my car.
sentences.zh: 比如，我的车上贴了拜登的贴纸。

sentences.en: I have never done that before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没这样做过。

sentences.en: Husband and I are in arguments about it still because he's all like, your car's going to get keyed, you know?
sentences.zh: 我和丈夫还在为此争论，因为他总是说，你的车会被人划伤的，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's not that he cares, of course, that, you know, I have my politics.
sentences.zh: 当然，他并不是不在乎我有自己的政治立场。

sentences.en: It's, you know, he's like, something's going to happen to the car, you know?
sentences.zh: 他只是，你知道，他担心车会出事。

sentences.en: Like, somebody's going to slash your tires.
sentences.zh: 比如，有人会划破你的轮胎。

sentences.en: But that hasn't happened.
sentences.zh: 但那并没有发生。

sentences.en: Instead, Andrea says her public support of Biden seems to be giving people a reason to connect with her, to open up about their own politics.
sentences.zh: 相反，安德里亚说她对拜登的公开支持似乎给了人们与她建立联系的理由，让他们愿意敞开心扉谈论自己的政治立场。

sentences.en: Having a sticker on my car, it has led to conversations with people who are then like, oh, you know, and so it's, I've been surprised, you know, that I have inspired some folks to
sentences.zh: 车上贴了贴纸，这引发了与人们的对话，他们会说，噢，你知道，所以我很惊讶，我竟然激励了一些人

sentences.en: get more involved.
sentences.zh: 参与进来。

sentences.en: I had so many regrets in 2016 because I took for granted that I just, I just thought Hillary would win.
sentences.zh: 2016年我有很多遗憾，因为我理所当然地认为，我只是觉得希拉里会赢。

sentences.en: I thought it would be no question.
sentences.zh: 我以为那是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: And so I've said since then, like, I'm not, I'm determined not to have regrets on November
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起我就说，我决心这次在11月4日

sentences.en: 4th this time.
sentences.zh: 那天不再有遗憾。

sentences.en: And I'm really just pushing myself so much to do everything I can.
sentences.zh: 我真的在竭尽全力做我能做的一切。

sentences.en: And so many times a day, Andrea, women in these final weeks who are just saying every day, I'm exhausted.
sentences.zh: 在这些最后的几周里，安德里亚，每天都有很多女性说，我精疲力竭。

sentences.en: This feels hard right now.
sentences.zh: 现在感觉很难。

sentences.en: But I don't want to feel the way I felt the day after the election last year or women who have changed in the meantime.
sentences.zh: 但我不想再有去年大选后那种感觉，也不想再有那些在此期间发生改变的女性那样的感觉。

sentences.en: I want this feeling to go away.
sentences.zh: 我想让这种感觉消失。

sentences.en: I want to be able to have the president on TV and it be OK that my kids are in the room.
sentences.zh: 我想在电视上看到总统时，孩子们在房间里也没关系。

sentences.en: There's just this stress and this sick feeling in the pits of our stomach that everyone wants to go away.
sentences.zh: 那种压力和胃里翻江倒海的恶心感，每个人都希望它消失。

sentences.en: I hear it every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都能听到。

sentences.en: Donald Trump may very well take Ohio again this year.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普今年很有可能再次拿下俄亥俄州。

sentences.en: Most polls show him slightly favored to win.
sentences.zh: 大多数民调显示他略占优势。

sentences.en: But that's not because suburban women here haven't changed their minds.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是因为这里的郊区女性没有改变主意。

sentences.en: The latest polling shows that the suburbs of Ohio are now acting like the suburbs in the rest of the country, with Biden leading by about 20 points here.
sentences.zh: 最新的民调显示，俄亥俄州的郊区现在的表现就像全国其他地区的郊区一样，拜登在这里领先约20个百分点。

sentences.en: But a question I've been having is, if Trump does lose, if that sick feeling in the pits of
sentences.zh: 但我一直有个疑问，如果特朗普真的输了，如果凯蒂所描述的那种胃里翻江倒海的恶心感

sentences.en: their stomach, as Katie describes it, goes away, will they go back to the lives they lived before?
sentences.zh: 消失了，她们会回到以前的生活吗？

sentences.en: Do you think you'll ever vote Republican again?
sentences.zh: 你认为你还会再投票给共和党吗？

sentences.en: You see a world where that could happen?
sentences.zh: 你能想象那种情况会发生吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think?
sentences.zh: 还是说你认为？

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I cannot imagine a Republican candidate that I would rally behind at this moment.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象此刻会有哪位共和党候选人能让我支持。

sentences.en: Hannah, the Gary Johnson voter, doesn't think so.
sentences.zh: 汉娜，那位曾投给加里·约翰逊的选民，并不这么认为。

sentences.en: I cannot even imagine what kind of values or rhetoric or kindness they could show that would make me think I could trust them.
sentences.zh: 我甚至无法想象他们能表现出什么样的价值观、言辞或善意，能让我觉得可以信任他们。

sentences.en: I have not even considered that until you said it.
sentences.zh: 在你提起之前，我甚至没考虑过这个问题。

sentences.en: And wow, that's mind-blowing.
sentences.zh: 哇，这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: To think that's a huge departure.
sentences.zh: 想到这是一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: I think Donald Trump has done so much damage in the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 我认为唐纳德·特朗普对共和党造成了太大的破坏。

sentences.en: I don't think I trust any of them.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我信任他们中的任何一个。

sentences.en: You'd have to wipe them all out and bring in new guys.
sentences.zh: 你得把他们全部清除，换上新人。

sentences.en: Wow.

sentences.zh: 这是一个发人深省的问题。

sentences.en: I don't think I would either, which isn't, you know, the same kind of wow question that it was for you, Hannah, but.
sentences.zh: 我想我也不会，虽然这不像对你来说那么令人震惊，汉娜，但是。

sentences.en: This is Andrea, the lifelong Republican who voted for Clinton.
sentences.zh: 这是安德里亚，那位曾投票给克林顿的终身共和党人。

sentences.en: The other piece of my journey is that, you know, Trump won in 2016.
sentences.zh: 我心路历程的另一部分是，你知道，特朗普在2016年赢了。

sentences.en: In 2017, I started my job at this school.
sentences.zh: 2017年，我开始在这所学校工作。

sentences.en: And 100% of the students at the school are on free and reduced lunch.
sentences.zh: 学校里100%的学生都享受免费或减价午餐。

sentences.en: And 99% of them are minorities.
sentences.zh: 而且99%是少数族裔。

sentences.en: They're students of color.
sentences.zh: 他们是有色人种学生。

sentences.en: So, you know, whereas before I had a lot of that more Republican ideology of, you know, hey, you have opportunities and you just need to work hard and make it happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，虽然以前我有更多那种共和党的意识形态，认为只要你有机会，努力工作就能成功。

sentences.en: Instead,
sentences.zh: 但相反，

sentences.en: I was seeing situations in which the DAC is really just truly stacked against folks and then also now being a lot more informed and starting to understand more about the laws and the policies that are really behind a lot of the Republican candidates.
sentences.zh: 我看到了现实情况，系统确实对人们非常不利，而且现在我了解得更多了，开始更多地理解共和党候选人背后真正的法律和政策。

sentences.en: It's I can't imagine myself going back to Republican Party ever either.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象自己还会回到共和党。

sentences.en: And then there's Kate, the Trump voter.
sentences.zh: 还有凯特，那位特朗普的支持者。

sentences.en: Yeah, if you had asked me in January, February, I probably would have said, like, no, I'm still pretty moderate.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你在1月、2月问我，我可能会说，不，我还是挺温和的。

sentences.en: Like, I can see myself being a swing voter.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己可能还是个摇摆选民。

sentences.en: However, like, there was so much that came to light after George Floyd with systemic racism, like the Republicans aren't doing anything to help it.
sentences.zh: 然而，乔治·弗洛伊德事件后，系统性种族主义暴露无遗，共和党人却什么都没做。

sentences.en: Donald Trump could be doing everything that he's doing now, but had the party resisted and, like, stepped up and spoken out, the lack of, you know, like,
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普可以继续做他现在做的一切，但如果党内有人抵制、站出来发声，那么这种对党派的

sentences.en: trust and belief in the party wouldn't have been loSt.
sentences.zh: 信任和信念就不会丧失。

sentences.en: But it is.
sentences.zh: 但它确实丧失了。

sentences.en: with a strong majority having a favorable view of the Black Lives Matter movement.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人对“黑人的命也是命”运动持正面看法。

sentences.en: And suburban voters in general expressing disapproval for how the president handled the protests and race relations.
sentences.zh: 郊区选民普遍对总统处理抗议活动和种族关系的方式表示不满。

sentences.en: And for these women, it connects to their roles as mothers.
sentences.zh: 对这些女性来说，这与她们作为母亲的角色有关。

sentences.en: George Floyd called out to his mom.
sentences.zh: 乔治·弗洛伊德呼唤了他的妈妈。

sentences.en: Like, that was a huge thing for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说意义重大。

sentences.en: Like, I really felt summoned to do more and make sure that my son wasn't going to turn out.
sentences.zh: 我真的感到被召唤去做更多的事情，确保我的儿子不会变成那样。

sentences.en: Like, for me, I was like, OK, I don't want to raise a, you know, cop that kills somebody, that murders someone.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我想的是，我不想养出一个杀人、谋杀别人的警察。

sentences.en: And that I needed to, you know, just do a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我需要多做一点点。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: I appreciate you mentioning the George Floyd and that calling out for his mama.
sentences.zh: 我很感激你提到乔治·弗洛伊德以及他呼唤妈妈的事。

sentences.en: Like, I saw signs.
sentences.zh: 我看到了标语。

sentences.en: Like, I still, like, get chills when I see that sign.
sentences.zh: 每当我看到那个标语，我依然会起鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: Like, he called out for all the mamas when he called out for his mama.
sentences.zh: 他呼唤妈妈时，其实是在呼唤所有的妈妈。

sentences.en: And it does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It gives me chills every time.
sentences.zh: 每次想起都让我起鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: Yeah, you called him an unspeakable force.
sentences.zh: 是的，你称他为一股不可言说的力量。

sentences.en: Because I'm not going to lie and say, like, in February, I was worried about racism in America.
sentences.zh: 因为我不会撒谎说，二月份时我还在担心美国的种族主义。

sentences.en: Like, I wasn't.
sentences.zh: 我当时并没有。

sentences.en: And I think it really, like, it blew the horn and brought the attention of so many women.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的吹响了号角，引起了这么多女性的关注。

sentences.en: As I'm listening to these women talk about George Floyd, it occurs to me that in the last four years, they didn't just switch parties.
sentences.zh: 当我听着这些女性谈论乔治·弗洛伊德时，我意识到在过去四年里，她们不仅仅是转换了党派。

sentences.en: They're talking about a deeper change in their values.
sentences.zh: 她们谈论的是价值观更深层的改变。

sentences.en: I think it was just more the things that were brought to light that I, as a very white, privileged, suburban woman, did not realize was a problem.
sentences.zh: 我想这更多是因为那些被揭露出来的事情，作为一个非常白人、有特权的郊区女性，我以前并没有意识到那是个问题。

sentences.en: Because it wasn't my problem.
sentences.zh: 因为那不是我的问题。

sentences.en: And needing to not only, like, acknowledge these problems, but we can't only be self-absorbed in our choices.
sentences.zh: 不仅需要承认这些问题，我们也不能只沉溺于自己的选择。

sentences.en: Like, I have to think of everybody.
sentences.zh: 我必须为每个人着想。

sentences.en: So, if I'm voting against Donald Trump, that's not a vote for me or a vote for my son.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我投票反对唐纳德·特朗普，那不是为了我自己或我的儿子。

sentences.en: That's a vote for, like, everyone's sons.
sentences.zh: 那是为了所有人的儿子投票。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: This is a pretty profound shift in voting behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常深刻的投票行为转变。

sentences.en: I asked Hannah, who in 2016 refused to vote for Hillary Clinton because of her position on abortion, whether her support for Biden means she's reconciled that.
sentences.zh: 我问汉娜，她在2016年因为堕胎立场拒绝投票给希拉里，现在支持拜登是否意味着她已经调和了这一点。

sentences.en: I wonder if there's something about how Biden approaches the issue that makes it easier for you.
sentences.zh: 我想知道拜登处理这个问题的方式是否让你更容易接受。

sentences.en: I don't know that, I don't know that Biden is the one that has changed my mind on it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，我不觉得是拜登改变了我的想法。

sentences.en: I've also seen examples in the lives of people close to me where it's, it's forced me, it's required me to complicate my understanding of the issue.
sentences.zh: 我也在身边人的生活中看到了例子，这迫使我、要求我让对这个问题的理解变得复杂化。

sentences.en: Where, as once it was a black and white issue of life and death, I've become aware of different medical conditions and different things that I'm embarrassed to say at 37 years old,
sentences.zh: 曾经这是一个非黑即白的生死问题，但我现在意识到了不同的医疗状况，以及一些我羞于启齿的事情，在37岁时，

sentences.en: I honestly didn't know.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道。

sentences.en: You know, I was out there with my fists in the air, pro-life, pro-life, and had no idea the repercussions of what I was saying and doing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾经挥舞着拳头，高喊反堕胎，却根本不知道我所说所做带来的后果。

sentences.en: Um, and I, there's people near and dear to me who have had really awful experiences.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我身边有亲近的人经历过非常糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: And that just makes me take a step back and realize that I don't really get a voice in the most intimate details of their life.
sentences.zh: 这让我退后一步意识到，在他们生活最私密的细节上，我并没有发言权。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I had a very similar journey on the abortion thing, too.
sentences.zh: 我在堕胎问题上也经历了非常相似的心路历程。

sentences.en: Andrea joins in.
